summary: Distribution Alpha entry criteria were defined as a runtime-foundation handoff contract. Alpha work is blocked from starting from the MVP boot skeleton alone and must inherit AgentCore, Security Execution Foundation, runtime artifact installation, persistent state directories, safety gates, release/provenance checks, and QEMU gates.

entry_contract.distribution_alpha_status: blocked until TASK-RTF-005 completes Runtime Foundation final audit
inherited_gates: approved and denied service recovery smoke when packaging changes touch runtime
QEMU dependency gate and full QEMU boot smoke when boot/rootfs/image factory changes affect handoff
entry_contract.firecracker_position: Alpha executor/isolation profile behind SecurityExecutionEngine, not a substitute for SEF or a parallel side-effect path
entry_contract.model_broker_rule: stub/local-only mode remains mandatory; external LLM providers are optional-only and cannot be required by acceptance tests

acceptance_evidence.distribution_alpha_cannot_start_from_mvp: docs/distribution-alpha-entry-criteria.md rejects a bootable Linux image with agentd binary as insufficient and blocks promotion until TASK-RTF-005.
acceptance_evidence.generic_service_recovery_required: entry criteria list generic AgentCore service recovery and TASK-ACR-009 as prerequisites for future Alpha packaging and VM image tasks.
acceptance_evidence.runtime_safety_gates_required: entry criteria inherit full regression, safety::, agent_core::, agent_core::adversarial, service recovery, audit projection, release/provenance, QEMU, and artifact hygiene gates.
acceptance_evidence.persistent_runtime_directories_and_artif: entry criteria define rootfs contracts for agentd, policy pack, semantic tool manifest, run-state, audit, rollback, ModelBroker config, memory, and release/provenance metadata.

verification.document_review: Distribution Alpha entry criteria document includes prerequisites, runtime artifacts, inherited gates, VM image factory prerequisite, Firecracker boundary, ModelBroker rule, and future task dependency rule.
